sonnet.problem: Story card 3 already says the psalmist "has sought His face." The true/false statement just repeats that and adds only "with all his heart." The prior card therefore gives away the answer.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: The right answer "To God's testimonies" is the only abstract, scriptural-sounding option. The wrong answers "Back toward home" and "Toward the temple" are physical places, so the right answer stands out and the answers are not the same kind of thing.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

sonnet.problem: The jokes repeat one punchline shape. Papa Dorin says "Friend, I..." and then compares his own baking or drawer life to what the psalmist just did. This happens in stop 2 cards 1, 5 and 9, and in stop 3 cards 8 and 11.
sonnet.rule: No formula. His personality fits whatever moment he's in... Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.
